name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Democrat Chris Rabb heavily outraises independent Dennis Mahoney
Prediction markets price Democratic win around 96%
Open seat after Dwight Evans' retirement
model.rationale: The D+40 fundamentals make this overwhelmingly Democratic territory, and Rabb's roughly $1.3 million raised plus $1.6 million in outside support dwarfs Mahoney's token operation. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays at a large Democratic margin.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or an unexpectedly well-funded independent campaign could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
This Philadelphia-area seat is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+40. Incumbent Dwight Evans is retiring, leaving an open seat that the party holding it is heavily favored to keep. State Representative Chris Rabb is the Democratic nominee and enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised about $1.3 million and benefited from roughly $1.6 million in outside support.

His main opponent, independent Dennis Mahoney, has raised only about $11,000 and shows no outside spending on his behalf. Prediction markets put the Democratic chance of winning around 96 percent. With no public polling and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic victory in the low double digits to thirty-point range.
